title: Recording of Retinal Action Potentials from Single Cells in the Insect Compound Eye
why: Copera: the second hit of the harvest query "Copera eye" (90 hits). The stored abstract says that electrical responses were recorded intracellularly from the compound eyes of a fly (Lucilia) and of several dragonflies (Copera, Agriocnemis and Lestes), describes the dragonfly ommatidium (four retinula cells and a rhabdom of three rhabdomeres) and a response of two phases, a transient spike-like potential and a slow potential maintained during illumination, and stops before the rest of the results. The full text may therefore give the time course or the flicker response of a Copera photoreceptor (cff_hz, corner_hz) or its responses to lights of different wavelengths (lambda_max_nm, spectral_range_nm). The abstract does not name the Copera species. It is the only work in the harvest or in the desk's web searches that reports a measurement on a Copera eye, and main holds no row from it. The web pairs for these traits ("Copera flicker fusion", "yellow bush dart flicker fusion", "Copera spectral sensitivity" and "yellow bush dart spectral sensitivity") returned human flicker, camera and patent pages, a Springer article (BF02160841) that earlier records on main identify as Dodt's 1954 flicker study, the van der Kooi et al. 2021 review, a darter (fish) page and records without titles (PubMed Central PMC1333798, PMC1357591 and PMC3627921, a Zoological Studies PDF in volume 31, a SOKENDAI record and an NSF record); none names a damselfly. Not opened.

title: Morphological traits of the eyes of Lepidoptera indicate selection for binocular vision in both diurnal butterflies and nocturnal moths
why: A preprint on the eye morphology of 2,730 specimens of 224 butterfly and moth species, sampled across a tribal-level phylogeny of butterflies and a genomic sampling of moths, which links eye features to detectability, resolution and stereopsis; its stored abstract start names no species, so whether its species list or data hold a species of these genera, and whether they give an acuity or an interommatidial angle (acuity_cpd, interommatidial_deg), is unseen. Main has logged eye-type, depth-cue and diel rows from its text and no acuity or angle, and several of main's wanted lists already hold it for other Lepidoptera. For this unit: Hesperia: the harvest's Hesperiidae vision review returned it (stored abstract start, no species named); the acuity pair ("Hesperia visual acuity", "branded skipper visual acuity") returned a French dictionary entry, patents, human acuity studies, the Wikipedia and StatPearls pages, Bologna and Tübingen catalogue records without titles and pages on vision in skiing and sport, and none names a skipper. Not opened.
get: green open access (Research Square preprint PDF from the harvest listing): https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-4203706/latest.pdf
